'''[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]'s 2001–02 season''' was the second under the presidency of [[Joan Gaspart]] and the single full season of management by [[Carles Rexach]] (who had replaced [[Lorenzo Serra Ferrer]] in the latter part of the [[2000–01 FC Barcelona season|previous campaign]]).

The summer of 2001 saw long-serving team captain [[Pep Guardiola|Josep Guardiola]] leave the club, while many transfer deals were concluded to give a new face to the squad with the signings of [[Roberto Bonano]], [[Javier Saviola]], [[Patrik Andersson]], [[Francesco Coco]], [[Geovanni Deiberson Maurício|Geovanni]], [[Philippe Christanval]] and [[Fábio Rochemback]]. This was also the final season at Barcelona of veteran players like [[Sergi Barjuán]], [[Abelardo Fernández|Abelardo]] and the talismanic [[Rivaldo]].

Barcelona had a mediocre campaign in [[La Liga]], finishing in 4th place, 11 points below eventual champions [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]; in Europe, on the other hand, they produced some very good performances, reaching the semi-finals of the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], where they were eliminated by [[El Clásico|fierce rivals]] (and eventual winners) [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. [[Patrick Kluivert]] was the club's top scorer in all competitions, with 25 goals.
